identity.name: QUEST
identity.tagline: Know where you stand. Know where to play.

pillar.also_pillar: P3 — Strategic & Organizational Impact (D6 AI Readiness connection)

identity.description: A 36-item executive capability assessment measuring performance across six dimensions: Strategic Thinking, Execution Excellence, Commercial Acumen, People Leadership, Adaptive Capacity, and AI Readiness. Leaders receive a composite executive readiness score, dimension-level verdicts, and a primary leadership archetype based on their highest-scoring capability dimensions.
identity.ideal_use_case: Executive readiness assessment for promotion or role expansion; leadership development programme intake; high-potential identification; executive coaching starting point; organisational leadership capability benchmarking.

instrument_spec.delivery_format: Online self-assessment with instant HTML report + optional consultant debrief
instrument_spec.scoring_method: Dimension-level normalised scores (0–20 each) + composite percentile (0–100)

dimensions.name: Strategic Thinking
dimensions.description: Measures the executive's ability to articulate direction, recognise patterns across market and competitive signals, hold multi-horizon perspectives, manage strategic assumptions, and translate strategy into actionable direction for their team.
dimensions.what_high_means: The executive can articulate precise strategic direction with trade-offs and time horizons, identifies patterns before peers, holds near-term and long-term views simultaneously, and actively monitors strategic assumptions.
dimensions.what_low_means: The executive struggles to explain how their work connects to broader strategy, may rely on others for direction-setting, and has difficulty articulating strategic trade-offs.

dimensions.name: Execution Excellence
dimensions.description: Measures the executive's ability to translate strategy into measurable results through organisational design, consistent delivery, performance tracking, clear accountability, and disciplined resource allocation.
dimensions.what_high_means: The executive builds structures that produce consistent results without their direct involvement, converts complex strategic goals into measurable outcomes on schedule, has early-warning systems for delivery risk, and makes disciplined resource trade-off decisions.
dimensions.what_low_means: The executive's team often misses commitments, execution is inconsistent, performance visibility is reactive rather than predictive, and resource allocation may favour political priorities over strategic value.

dimensions.name: Commercial Acumen
dimensions.description: Measures the executive's understanding of how the organisation creates and captures value, financial literacy, commercial decision-making under uncertainty, and APAC market-specific commercial intelligence.
dimensions.what_high_means: The executive can articulate the value creation mechanism with precision, is comfortable with financial data, makes credible commercial decisions under uncertainty, and understands specific APAC commercial dynamics.
dimensions.what_low_means: The executive finds commercial and financial conversations difficult, relies on finance colleagues to interpret data, and may lack confidence in commercial decision-making under uncertainty.

dimensions.name: People Leadership
dimensions.description: Measures the executive's ability to build strong teams, develop successors, create team independence, make individualised development investments, and navigate high-stakes people decisions while maintaining trust.
dimensions.what_high_means: The executive builds teams stronger than the sum of individuals, develops successors with clear trajectories, teams perform well in their absence, tailors leadership to individuals, and navigates difficult people decisions while preserving team trust.
dimensions.what_low_means: The executive tends to be the primary decision-maker, team performance drops when they are absent, succession pipeline is weak, and people decisions may be avoided or handled poorly.

dimensions.name: Adaptive Capacity
dimensions.description: Measures the executive's ability to identify and respond to environmental shifts, pivot strategy when needed, operate effectively in ambiguity, lead through APAC market and regulatory changes, and maintain course discipline while adapting.
dimensions.what_high_means: The executive identifies strategic implications of market shifts before peers, successfully pivots initiatives mid-execution without losing stakeholder confidence, performs well in ambiguity, and has led through major APAC landscape shifts.
dimensions.what_low_means: The executive performs best in stable environments, struggles with ambiguity, may resist changing course even when new information warrants it, and may be slow to respond to market or regulatory shifts.

dimensions.name: AI Readiness
dimensions.description: Measures the executive's readiness to lead in an AI-augmented environment — including AI decision architecture, data governance accountability, AI ethics and risk oversight, and organisational AI adoption change leadership.
dimensions.what_high_means: The executive has clear frameworks for AI-informed vs. human decisions, understands data governance obligations for AI, holds accountability for AI ethics and risk, and has led organisational AI adoption initiatives.
dimensions.what_low_means: The executive relies primarily on technical colleagues for AI governance, may not understand AI-related accountability structures, and has not actively led AI adoption in their organisation.
dimensions.cross_pillar_note: This dimension bridges P1 (Talent Pipeline Health — executive readiness) and P3 (Strategic & Organizational Impact — board-level AI governance).

archetype_framework.logic: Archetypes are determined by the leader's highest-scoring dimension pairs, classified by performance band (Advanced = 75+/100, Developing = 50–74, Emerging = <50). The Specialist is a single-dimension-dominant profile. The Seedling is a multi-low-dimension emerging profile.

band_levels.advanced: 75–100 composite — operating at senior executive level

archetypes.name: The Architect
archetypes.core_pattern: Designs robust systems and can pivot them when context changes. Rare combination at senior executive level.
archetypes.core_strength: Designs robust systems and can pivot them when context changes. Rare combination at senior executive level.
strengths: Exceptional strategic thinking — direction, pattern recognition, multi-horizon perspective
Strong adaptive capacity — pivots effectively, tolerates ambiguity, leads through change
Can design for the long term while adapting to the present
Rare combination of strategic depth and adaptive agility
growth_areas: Over-engineering risk — may design systems that are too complex for execution
Perfectionism slowing delivery — pursuing optimal at the cost of timely
May underinvest in commercial urgency — strategy over speed-to-market
Delegation discipline — may want to control the design too closely
archetypes.development_priority: Delegation discipline; 'good enough' calibration; commercial acumen deepening.
archetypes.key_risk: Over-engineering; perfectionism slowing delivery; may underinvest in commercial urgency

archetypes.name: The Catalyst
archetypes.core_pattern: Thrives in complexity and disruption; spots commercial opportunities others miss; acts fast.
archetypes.core_strength: Thrives in complexity and disruption; spots commercial opportunities others miss; acts fast.
strengths: Strong commercial acumen — value creation, financial literacy, market intelligence
Exceptional adaptive capacity — pivots fast, thrives in uncertainty
Bold commercial moves in rapidly changing markets
Sees opportunities others miss and acts on them quickly
growth_areas: Impatience with process and governance — may move too fast for organisational capacity
Risk of burning out teams — pace can exceed team absorption capacity
May deprioritise people development for commercial results
Can create quality issues if speed consistently overrides rigour
archetypes.development_priority: Sustainability mindset; team development investment; governance discipline.
archetypes.key_risk: Impatience with process and governance; may burn out teams; can deprioritise people development

archetypes.name: The Diplomat
archetypes.core_pattern: Builds coalitions, navigates politics, aligns diverse stakeholders around complex strategy.
archetypes.core_strength: Builds coalitions, aligns diverse stakeholders around complex strategy, and maintains strong people relationships.
strengths: Strong strategic thinking — can articulate direction and connect it to broader context
Exceptional people leadership — team architecture, succession, individualised development
Builds coalitions across diverse stakeholder groups
Maintains trust through strategic changes and difficult decisions
growth_areas: May prioritise harmony over hard decisions — people-pleaser tendency
Can be slow to confront underperformance — protecting relationship over standards
Execution rigour may be weaker than relationship and strategic capability
Commercial acumen may be underdeveloped — strong on people, weaker on P&L
archetypes.development_priority: Decisiveness under pressure; constructive confrontation capability; execution rigour.
archetypes.key_risk: May prioritise harmony over hard decisions; can be slow to confront underperformance

archetypes.name: The Commander
archetypes.core_pattern: Delivers results through commercial discipline and operational rigour; highly credible in P&L conversations.
archetypes.core_strength: Delivers results through commercial discipline and operational rigour; highly credible in P&L conversations.
strengths: Exceptional execution — consistent delivery, accountability architecture, resource discipline
Strong commercial acumen — financial literacy, value creation understanding, commercial confidence
Highly credible in P&L and results conversations
Reliable — delivers what they commit to
growth_areas: May neglect people development for short-term results — results-first mindset
Can be directive at the expense of team capability-building — telling over developing
Strategic thinking may be narrower — strong on execution, weaker on direction-setting
Adaptive capacity may lag — strong in stable execution contexts, less so in disruptive ones
archetypes.development_priority: People leadership investment; long-term talent pipeline thinking; adaptive capacity.
archetypes.key_risk: May neglect people development for short-term results; can be directive at the expense of team capability-building

archetypes.name: The Steward
archetypes.core_pattern: Guides teams through change with empathy and consistency; preserves team cohesion in uncertainty.
archetypes.core_strength: Guides teams through change with empathy and consistency; preserves team cohesion in uncertainty.
strengths: Strong adaptive capacity — leads through change, tolerates ambiguity
Good people leadership — maintains team cohesion during transitions
Empathetic and consistent leadership through uncertainty
Preserves morale and team stability in difficult contexts
growth_areas: May lack strategic direction or commercial edge — change leadership without clear destination
Decision conviction may be weaker — strong on process, less confident on direction
Strategic thinking sharpness may need development
Commercial acumen may be underdeveloped for senior roles
archetypes.development_priority: Strategic thinking sharpness; commercial acumen; decision conviction.
archetypes.key_risk: May lack strategic direction or commercial edge; change leadership without destination clarity
archetypes.note: Previously named 'The Navigator' in engine config. Renamed because 'navigate' is a banned word. 'The Steward' captures the same team-through-change pattern with a more accurate framing — they preserve and guide, they don't navigate.

archetypes.name: The Strategist
archetypes.core_pattern: Sees the big picture clearly; excellent at analysis and direction-setting.
archetypes.core_strength: Sees the big picture clearly; excellent at analysis and direction-setting.
strengths: Strong strategic thinking — clear direction, pattern recognition, multi-horizon perspective
Excellent analysis and direction-setting capability
Can articulate complex strategy clearly
Strong at identifying assumptions and strategic linkages
growth_areas: Execution gaps — vision without delivery mechanism
May rely on others for follow-through and implementation
Team mobilisation capability may be weaker than analysis capability
Accountability architecture may be underdeveloped
archetypes.development_priority: Execution Excellence; team mobilisation; accountability architecture.
archetypes.key_risk: Execution gaps — vision without delivery mechanism; may rely on others for follow-through

archetypes.name: The Engine
archetypes.core_pattern: Reliable delivery machine; consistent output; operationally credible.
archetypes.core_strength: Reliable delivery machine; consistent output; operationally credible.
strengths: Strong execution — reliable delivery, consistent output, operational credibility
Good organisational design and accountability structures
Operationally credible — knows how to get things done
Resource discipline — makes tough allocation decisions
growth_areas: May be executing the wrong strategy — strong delivery, weaker direction
Tends to optimise the current path rather than question it
Strategic thinking may be underdeveloped
Commercial awareness and adaptive capacity may lag
archetypes.development_priority: Strategic thinking; commercial awareness; adaptive capacity.
archetypes.key_risk: May be executing the wrong strategy; tends to optimise the current path rather than question it

archetypes.name: The Entrepreneur
archetypes.core_pattern: Bold commercial moves; market-savvy; pivots fast when opportunity shifts.
archetypes.core_strength: Bold commercial moves; market-savvy; pivots fast when opportunity shifts.
strengths: Strong commercial acumen — market-savvy, opportunity-spotting, commercial judgment
Good adaptive capacity — pivots fast when opportunity shifts
Bold commercial moves and risk-taking
Entrepreneurial energy and initiative
growth_areas: May lack organisational buy-in or people development capability
Governance gaps — may move faster than organisational controls can handle
People leadership may be underdeveloped — strong on opportunity, weaker on team building
Execution discipline may be inconsistent — strong on start-up, weaker on scale-up
archetypes.development_priority: People leadership; execution discipline; stakeholder management.
archetypes.key_risk: May lack organisational buy-in or people development capability; governance gaps

archetypes.name: The Specialist
strength_dimensions: One dimension dominant (>15 pts above all others)
archetypes.core_pattern: Deep expertise in one executive capability domain; highly valued for that specific strength.
archetypes.core_strength: Deep expertise in one executive capability domain; highly valued for that specific strength.
strengths: Exceptional depth in one capability domain
Highly valued for specific expertise
Clear personal brand and value proposition
Can serve as go-to expert in their area of strength
growth_areas: Over-reliance on single strength — may have blind spots in 2–3 other dimensions
Seniority ceiling may be limited by breadth of capability
Risk of becoming a specialist leader rather than a general executive
May struggle in roles requiring broader capability set
archetypes.development_priority: Broadening capability across secondary dimensions; delegation of dominant strength to create capacity.
archetypes.key_risk: Over-reliance on single strength; may have blind spots in 2–3 other dimensions that limit seniority ceiling

archetypes.name: The Seedling
archetypes.core_pattern: High development potential; early in the executive capability journey; typically high motivation.
archetypes.core_strength: High development potential; early in the executive capability journey; typically high motivation.
strengths: Often high motivation and learning appetite
Early in journey — substantial growth runway
Can develop rapidly with structured support
Potential to grow into any archetype with the right development
growth_areas: Overwhelm risk — pursuing development in too many areas simultaneously
Wrong sequencing of priorities — trying to build everything at once
Multiple capability gaps across executive dimensions
May not yet know which strengths to build around
archetypes.development_priority: Focus on 1–2 highest-leverage dimensions only; structured mentoring; SHIFT-QUEST programme indicated.
archetypes.key_risk: Overwhelm; pursuing development in too many areas simultaneously; wrong sequencing of priorities

composite_scoring.method: Six-dimension average of normalised scores, converted to 0–100 composite

bands.interpretation: Strong capability across all six dimensions; operating at senior executive level.
1–2 capability gaps to address; strong foundation with targeted development needed.
Substantive development needed in 2–3 dimensions; structured programme recommended.
In transition to executive level; not yet operating at full capability.
Fundamental capability gaps; foundational development required.

dimension_verdicts.meaning: Deployable capability; executive operates at this level consistently and under pressure
Functional in stable conditions; gaps emerge under pressure or in unfamiliar APAC contexts
Underdeveloped for the executive's current or target role; primary development priority

report_output.report_format: Interactive HTML report with visual capability profile + optional consultant debrief

source_engine_drift.note: Engine full_name was an invented official-sounding name containing banned word 'Architecture'; canonical name follows NAME — descriptor format per Messaging Canon v1.0
'Navigator' derives from banned word 'navigate'. 'The Steward' captures the same core pattern (guides teams through change, preserves cohesion) with appropriate terminology.
Minor threshold discrepancy between engine (16) and QB (15). Engine config is scoring source of truth. User-facing verdicts should align with actual scoring thresholds used in production.
source_engine_drift.resolution: Using engine config thresholds (16/10) as canonical for scoring; description language ('Strength' vs 'Strong') follows whichever is the active UI standard.
